webority-db-migrator - shared schema runner (DbUp), SQL Server or PostgreSQL

Usage:
  webority-db-migrator --connection "<conn>" [options]

Options:
  --connection, -c <string>   Connection string (or set MIGRATOR_CONNECTION env var)
  --provider, -p <db>         sqlserver (default) or postgres
  --db-root, -r <dir>         DB project folder with Scripts/ and/or StoredProcedures/ (default: .)
  --what-if, -w               List pending run-once scripts, run the applied-script guard below,
                              and exit. Changes nothing.
  --mark-applied, -m          Baseline: record existing run-once scripts as applied WITHOUT executing
  --force, -f                 Allow --mark-applied against a DB whose journal already has entries
                              (only valid with --mark-applied)
  --tx-per-script, -x         Wrap each script in its own transaction (default: off)
  --timeout, -t <seconds>     Per-script command timeout (default: 600)
  --accept-checksum <name>    Accept the current content of one already-applied script (repeatable)
  --help, -h                  Show this help and exit

The applied-script guard:
  Every run-once script's content is hashed into SchemaVersions.Checksum when it is applied. On a
  later run, a script whose content no longer matches its stored hash fails the run, because an
  applied script is immutable by convention and an edit to one is silently ignored on every
  database that already ran it.

  Line endings and a trailing newline are ignored, so the same script on Windows and Linux agrees.
  If the change IS intended, review it and accept it by journal name:

    --accept-checksum 20260101_0900_AddColumn.sql

  That rewrites the stored hash for that one script from the file on disk, printing the old and new
  values. There is deliberately no switch to turn the guard off everywhere.

What the command line will not accept:
  A bare word with no option in front of it, so a connection string passed without --connection
  stops the run instead of being dropped in
